Package com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules

Class CtaValidationRule

java.lang.Object
com.acxiom.emailaudit.rules.CtaValidationRule
All Implemented Interfaces:
AuditRule
public final class CtaValidationRule extends Object implements AuditRule
AuditRule that validates primary call-to-action (CTA) elements — <button> elements, <a> elements styled to look like buttons, and <a> elements wrapping a single CTA image — on a rendered HTML page.

Why this matters

A CTA is the single most important interactive element in most marketing emails. A CTA that is invisible, has no destination, or has no readable label is a silent conversion-killer: it looks correct to a developer reviewing markup but fails completely for the recipient.

CTA detection

An element is treated as a CTA candidate if it is:

  • any <button> element, or
  • any <a> element that is styled as a button, determined by any of:
    • role="button", or
    • a class attribute containing "btn" or "button" (case-insensitive), or
    • a computed style with both a non-transparent background-color and non-zero padding — the visual hallmark of a button in HTML email markup, where <a> tags are styled with inline padding/background rather than using native <button> elements.
  • or any <a> element that wraps a single <img> and has no visible text of its own — the "image button" pattern used throughout HTML email, where a raster CTA graphic (e.g. <a href="..."><img src="cta_join_now.png" alt="Join now"></a>) stands in for native button markup. Without this branch, image-only CTAs are invisible to this rule entirely: they have no text, no role="button", no btn class, and typically no background/padding on the anchor itself (padding is usually applied to a wrapping <td> in email markup), so the previous detector never matched them — meaning the rule always reported PASS on zero checked elements regardless of whether the CTA's destination was broken, hidden, or unlabeled.

Visible text for image-button CTAs

For an image-button CTA, "visible text" is taken from the wrapped image's alt attribute when the anchor itself has no text content — this mirrors what a screen reader announces for the element and lets the existing empty-text check correctly flag image buttons with missing or empty alt text as a real accessibility failure, rather than silently skipping them.

Checks performed

For every detected CTA candidate:

  • Empty text — the element's effective visible text (its own text, or its wrapped image's alt text) is empty.
  • Missing href — applies only to <a> elements: the href attribute is absent or empty. <button> elements are not required to have an href.
  • Hidden — the element's computed display is none, visibility is hidden, or opacity is 0.

A single CTA may produce more than one finding if it has multiple issues (e.g. a hidden button with no text).

PASS evidence

When the rule passes, it also returns one evidence finding per valid CTA candidate via FindingFormatter.linkFinding(), so the dashboard can show exactly which CTAs were reviewed and confirmed functional, e.g.:

 CTA Validation
   Displayed Text  : Shop Now
   Destination     : https://brand.com/shop
   Validation      : PASSED
   Reason          : CTA is visible with valid text and href

<button> elements (which have no href to validate) report "(not applicable)" as the destination, mirroring the FAIL-path convention already used in buildFindings(List).

Scope note

This rule intentionally does not distinguish a "primary" marketing CTA from other image-only links (e.g. a header logo link or a footer social icon) — any <a> wrapping exactly one image with no other text now qualifies as a candidate. In practice this only ever widens PASS-evidence coverage for those incidental links (they have a valid href and non-empty alt text, so they simply pass); it does not introduce false failures. If tighter precision is needed later (e.g. only treating CTA-named images as primary CTAs), that should be driven by an explicit include/exclude list rather than filename heuristics.

DOM and Playwright usage

CTA detection, text extraction, and computed-style checks are all performed via a single Page.evaluate(String) round-trip using window.getComputedStyle, leveraging Playwright's rendered page — not the raw HTML source — so styles applied via <style> blocks or external stylesheets are correctly reflected.

Thread safety

This class is stateless and has no mutable fields. It is safe for concurrent use from multiple TestNG threads, each operating on its own Page.
